title: How to Make Fire with Friction (Bow Drill Method)
summary: A vital primitive survival technique to create fire using dry branches and cordage without matches or lighters. Sawing the bow back and forth rapidly spins the center spindle, generating 400°C glowing coal dust through friction. Transferring this coal into a dry tinder nest and blowing gently ignites an open 600°C flame.

materials.name: Bow Stick & Heavy-Duty Cord
materials.desc: A 60-70cm slightly curved sturdy branch lashed with tough wild vine cord or rawhide string to drive the spindle.

materials.name: Center Spindle Stick (Drill)
materials.desc: A thumb-thick (2cm diameter), 25cm long straight bone-dry wooden rod tapered to a pencil point on the lower friction tip.

materials.name: Hearth Board & Dry Tinder Nest
materials.desc: A 1.5-2cm thick flat dry softwood board paired with a bird's-nest bundle of dry grass and reed down to catch the ember.

steps.title: Step 1: Carve a 45-degree V-notch in the hearth board
steps.description:
1. **Spindle Socket Seating**: Press and spin the drill tip **1-1.5cm inward** from the hearth board edge to burn in a small circular depression.
2. **45-Degree V-Notch Carving**: Use a stone knife to slice a pizza-wedge-shaped **45-degree V-notch** from the board edge directly to the socket center.
3. **Base Collector Placement**: Tuck a flat, dry wide leaf directly beneath the notch to catch all falling hot carbon dust.
steps.actionNote: > Notch Alignment: The apex of the V-notch must touch the exact center of the drill hole. If misaligned, hot wood dust cannot exit and gets trapped around the spindle, preventing ember formation.
svgLabels: Notch apex must touch spindle axis center

deepDive.title: V-Notch Oxygen Draft & Carbon Dust Coalescence Dynamics
deepDive.text: Inside a round closed socket, lack of airflow suffocates carbonization. The 45-degree wedge notch creates an aerodynamic vent that draws in fresh oxygen while channeling **400°C+ pulverized charcoal** into a dense, self-insulating pile that coalesces into a living ember.

steps.title: Step 2: Press down with body weight and saw the bow full length
steps.description:
1. **Single Cord Wrap**: Wrap the bowstring **once completely around** the spindle to maintain tight, non-slip friction.
2. **12-15kg Downward Pressure**: Step firmly on the hearth board with your left foot and press down on the spindle top with a bearing block using **12-15kg of vertical body weight**.
3. **Full-Stroke Sawing**: Keep the bow horizontal and saw back and forth using the full length of the stick. Start smooth and steady.
4. **Smoke Acceleration Burst**: When thick white smoke billows out, accelerate to maximum effort for the **final 5 seconds with 15+ rapid strokes**.
steps.actionNote: > Thermal Threshold: Never stop at the first trace of smoke. You must maintain 10-15 powerful acceleration strokes after dense smoke appears to cross the 400°C ignition threshold.

deepDive.title: Mechanical Friction Conversion and 400°C Carbonization Limit
deepDive.text: Reciprocating kinetic energy from the bow converts instantaneously into thermal heat at the microscopic contact point. Wood begins charring at **250°C**, but sustained self-heating coals require the contact interface to surpass **400°C** under dense packing.

steps.title: Step 3: Transfer ember into tinder nest and elevate 45 degrees to ignite
steps.description:
1. **Ember Coalescence Delay**: Stop sawing and let the smoking black dust rest untouched on the base leaf for **30 seconds** until it fuses into a solid glowing coal.
2. **Tinder Nest Deposition**: Form dry grass into a cup-shaped bird's nest and gently dump the ember block into the core.
3. **45-Degree Elevation**: Hold the nest at a **45-degree angle** slightly above eye level and blow **long, gentle breaths** directly into the coal.
4. **Flame Flashover**: Oxygen fans the glow until an open **600°C flame** bursts within **15-20 seconds**; immediately transfer to your prepared campfire kindling.
steps.actionNote: > Updraft Angle Rule: Holding the tinder nest at a 45-degree elevation prevents smoke from stinging your eyes while convective updrafts preheat surrounding fibers, doubling ignition reliability.

deepDive.title: Convective Heat Transfer and 600°C Flame Phase Transition
deepDive.text: The 450°C coal is a solid-state smoldering mass. Supplying a laminar stream of gentle oxygen drives off volatile carbon monoxide and wood gases. As local temperature exceeds **600°C**, gas-phase combustion takes over, erupting into a self-sustaining open flame.

fatalMistake.title: Critical Mistake: Blowing rashly on loose, freshly formed ember dust
fatalMistake.description: Blowing hard on the black dust immediately after stopping will blow the uncoalesced particles away, scattering heat and extinguishing the core instantaneously.
fatalMistake.consequence: Remedy: When smoke rises from the dust pile, wait 30 seconds for the embers to fuse into a solid glowing coal before transferring to tinder.

outcome.title: Completed Bow Drill Friction Fire & Ember Ignition
outcome.description: A glowing 400°C charcoal ember generated in the 45° V-notch smoking heavily, transferred safely into a dry tinder nest and fanned into an open flame.
